interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins and the absence of seminal vesicle invasion and lymph node metastasis. The preoperative PSA was 3.7. Conversely, the surgical pathology noted a Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5) and pathological T3a stage, which contributes to risk. The absence of lymph node metastasis is a positive finding. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as missing, which widens uncertainty regarding the true extent of disease. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data prevents a definitive assessment of the subsequent trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent changes would significantly revise this prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 36 months without an event. The fixed estimated horizon is 36.15 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 27.12–45.19 months; its coverage has not been validated.
